Accommodation possibilities for Incoming Students – How to find somewhere to live 
This document contains information and tips for incoming students at the ZHAW who are look-
ing for somewhere to live. 
1. Student Housing Cooperative 
WOKO (Studentische Wohngenossenschaft Zürich) offers inexpensive accommodation for stu-
dents. Link to WOKO 
If you are interested in WOKO accommodation, please notify the ZHAW Registrar’s Office as 
soon as you are accepted as a visiting student. There are a limited number of housing possibili-
ties and the “first come, first served” principle applies. Registration is binding; in the case of 
withdrawal, costs will be incurred. 
2. Searching independently  
There are a limited number of rooms and flats on the market and there is a lot of competition, so 
you should start searching well in advance, check for new additions on a daily basis, and apply 
immediately.  
Don’t limit your search to the centres of Winterthur and Zurich. Many smaller towns and villages 
are only half an hour away on public transport, and it often costs less to rent places outside the 
city centres. You can check the distance to the ZHAW by going to sbb.ch, zvv.ch or 
map.search.ch

2.2 Newspapers and notice boards 
Once you are in Switzerland, it is worth checking the notice boards of local universities (ETH, 
University of Zürich, ZHAW). 
Advertisements in newspapers are also a good source. Almost all local papers publish accom-
modation advertisements on a regular basis. The most well-known newspapers in the Win-
terthur and Zurich area are: “Der Landbote”, “Winterthurer Zeitung”, “WOZ Die Wochenzeitung”, 
“Zürcher Unterländer”, “Tagblatt der Stadt Zürich”, “Tages-Anzeiger” and the “Neue Zürcher Zei-
tung”.  
Rooms in shared student flats rarely appear in newspapers and can usually be found on notice 
boards at the universities.  
It is not always easy for foreign visiting students to rent a flat of their own. Sometimes residency 
permits, deposits, contractually agreed renting periods, etc. are demanded. 
2.3 Networking 
Use your own personal contacts with colleagues or other students, even before you arrive in 
Switzerland. Ask students in your home country who have been in Switzerland for help before 
you come, for example.  
Student organisations such as ESN or Alias ZHAW might be useful too. And there are also 
ZHAW students who want to rent out their own accommodation while they are studying abroad. 
2.4 Homestays 
Students who wish to experience Swiss lifestyle, culture and language by living in a family 
should consider homestays. The following platforms offer assistance in finding a suitable host 
family: 
 
 
http://www.homestayweb.com 
 
https://www.couchsurfing.com 
http://www.worldhomestay.com http://homestaybooking.de 
http://www.workaway.info  
 
3. ZHAW emergency number 
If you find yourself in a threatening situation during your stay, or if you witness such a situation, 
please call the ZHAW emergency number: +41(0)58 934 70 70 (round the clock). Detailed in-
formation can be found at: https://www.zhaw.ch/en/about-us/emergencies/.
